page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.large is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is anchored by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor offering 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local temporary storage is integrated directly via a 75 GB NVMe SSD volume, eliminating the need for attached block storage for temporary data needs. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and the configuration contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight predictable single-core capability paired with throughput ceilings imposed by the dual-vCPU count. The instance registers an average Geekbench single-core score of 1188.0, whereas multi-core benchmark performance settles at 1416.0. Memory throughput reaches 96.13 GB/sec under cached small-block reads, reducing to 13.84 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 11.61 GB/sec for large-block writes. Application-level metrics reflect 1.7 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 1.97 GB/sec in static web throughput testing.

Resource density tradeoffs stem from the single physical core allocation, which restricts highly concurrent workloads and compute-heavy compilation pipelines. However, bundled local NVMe storage provides low-latency disk access and high qualitative cost efficiency for scratch space requirements. The architecture serves workloads such as small relational databases, memory caching servers, automated CI/CD worker nodes, and basic web serving where direct local drive performance is beneficial.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.large is a general-purpose Nitro instance configured with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL core operating at 3.1 GHz. The hardware profile includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, a dedicated 75 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and a baseline network capacity of 2 Gbps. While single-thread responsiveness achieves solid mid-range performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 1188.0, overall multi-core computational density is limited by the single physical core allocation. Memory bandwidth tests measure 13.84 GB/sec for uncached reads, while Redis operations reach 1.7 million SET operations per second. The integration of high-speed local NVMe storage improves qualitative efficiency for I/O-sensitive operations without requiring auxiliary block storage attachments. This configuration is well matched for lightweight web hosting, small transactional databases, local cache proxies, and development environments that benefit from direct high-speed scratch disk access.
